payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Abigail, In, Kayleen, Serina

payload.content: Hi team — Abigail here (avail 4.0h; skills security 0.83, devops 0.68). My cheapest feasible tasks are the medium-priority ISSUE-0002 items and the low-priority ISSUE-0001 triage/review/docs. To avoid duplicates, I plan to claim ISSUE-0002::review (my cost 3.51, medium priority, fits my devops+security skills). Could each of you reply with which task you intend to take so we cover 4 distinct tasks? If someone else strongly prefers ISSUE-0002::review, I can fall back to ISSUE-0001::triage or ISSUE-0001::review.

Kayleen here (avail 4.0h; devops 0.77). My private costs, cheapest first: ISSUE-0001::triage=2.77 (low), ISSUE-0001::review=3.47, ISSUE-0001::docs=3.47 (low), ISSUE-0001::test=5.05 (low), ISSUE-0002::review=6.21 (med), ISSUE-0002::test=8.90 (med), ISSUE-0001::implement=8.93 (low), ISSUE-0002::implement=14.43 (med). Since the medium ISSUE-0002 items are expensive for me, I plan to claim ISSUE-0001::triage (cost 2.77, 2.4h — well within my availability). Abigail, go ahead with ISSUE-0002::review. @In, @Serina — please post which distinct task you'll take (ideally one of the medium ISSUE-0002 items if your security/devops match is good), so we cover 4 distinct tasks with no duplicates. I can flex to ISSUE-0001::review/docs if someone else needs triage.

Serina here (avail 7.0h; devops 0.82). My private costs, cheapest first: ISSUE-0001::triage=2.62, ISSUE-0001::review=3.27, ISSUE-0001::docs=3.27, ISSUE-0001::test=4.58, ISSUE-0002::review=5.90 (med), ISSUE-0001::implement=6.54, ISSUE-0002::test=8.26 (med), ISSUE-0002::implement=11.80 (med).

Given Abigail → ISSUE-0002::review and Kayleen → ISSUE-0001::triage, I'll claim a distinct medium task to lift priority coverage. My plan: ISSUE-0002::test (cost 8.26, devops+security, fits my devops 0.82). @In — please take ISSUE-0002::implement if your devops/security match is decent, otherwise a low ISSUE-0001 item (e.g. docs/review/test). That would give us 4 distinct tasks: 0002::review (med), 0002::test (med), 0002::implement (med), 0001::triage (low) → priority_sum 1.75 with no duplicates. If In strongly prefers 0002::test, I can flex down to ISSUE-0001::test or ISSUE-0001::review. Please confirm. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Update: locking in my intent unless @In objects — I'll take ISSUE-0002::test (medium, cost 8.26). Final proposed allocation: Abigail=ISSUE-0002::review, Kayleen=ISSUE-0001::triage, Serina=ISSUE-0002::test, In=ISSUE-0002::implement (or any remaining distinct low item if 0002::implement is too costly). This yields 4 distinct tasks, 3 of them medium priority, no duplicates. @In please confirm your pick so we avoid a duplicate claim. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Abigail confirming: I will claim ISSUE-0002::review (medium, effort 3.0 ≤ my 4.0h availability, cost 3.51, matches my devops+security skills). Agreed allocation stands: Abigail=ISSUE-0002::review, Kayleen=ISSUE-0001::triage, Serina=ISSUE-0002::test, In=ISSUE-0002::implement (or a remaining distinct low item if 0002::implement exceeds your availability/effort budget — just don't duplicate). @In please confirm your pick so we lock 4 distinct tasks with no duplicates.
